title: output-policy-layer-and-function-call-fence-openai-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces an output policy layer that enforces JSON schema contracts at streaming checkpoints and fences function/tool-call emissions; includes OpenAI adapter mappings for clearer error codes. Rolling update behind feature-flag with compatibility toggle.
description:
Motivation: Users integrating structured outputs and function calls need clearer, deterministic guarantees when streaming and when tool calls are emitted. Currently we have ad-hoc schema checks at the end of a response which leads to silent failures or expensive re-rolls for streaming clients. This PR introduces an output policy layer that participates in the streaming path to validate increments against a declared JSON schema, plus a "function-call fence" that prevents malformed tool-call payloads from being emitted downstream. The change also updates the OpenAI-compat adapter mapping so clients get actionable, stable error codes and suggestions for recovery.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds an Output Policy component to the runtime which can be configured per-request via response_format.schema and response_format.mode. The policy runs lightweight streaming checkpoints (schema latching) and can either annotate, buffer-and-repair, or abort depending on mode.
- Implements a Function Call Fence in the tool-calling pipeline that validates the function payload shape against the declared function schema before any side-effecting emission. If the fence trips, the runtime returns a structured diagnostic and prevents the call from reaching executors.
- Exposes a compat layer in api/openai_adapter to translate policy failures into OpenAI-compatible error payloads (with new error_type codes: schema_violation, function_fence, stream_checkpoint_failed). These payloads include guidance (retry with mode=permissive, attach failing token range, etc.) to help SDKs implement automated recovery.
- Adds a feature flag (runtime.output_policy.enabled) and a request-level toggle (response_format.mode) with values: permissive | warn | enforce. Existing clients default to permissive to preserve behavior.

Design notes:
- Streaming checks are implemented as checkpoints at sentence/JSON-boundary heuristics to minimize per-token overhead; the policy uses the same compiled validator as the final validation step to avoid drift.
- Buffer-and-repair attempts a single repair pass using the existing coercion helpers; we avoid iterative retries in this PR to keep latency predictable.
- Function-call fence hooks into the tool-call serializer; validation happens before any K/V caching or dispatch to external executors. This prevents partial side effects if a payload later fails validation.

Files touched (high level): crates/runtime/src/output_policy.rs, crates/runtime/src/streaming/checkpoint.rs, api/openai_adapter/response_mapper.py, api/openai_adapter/errors.py, sdk/python/redwood/schema_client.py, docs/response_format.md, tests/integration/test_stream_policy.py, tests/unit/test_function_fence.rs, infra/feature_flags/flags.yaml, examples/structured-output/annotated-example.json

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime output policy implementation with unit tests
- [x] Function call fence and unit tests
- [x] OpenAI adapter error mappings + tests
- [x] End-to-end streaming integration test (CI flaky capture added)
- [x] Docs for response_format.mode and migration guidance

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover validator wiring and fence rejection cases.
- Integration test simulates a streaming response where the generated JSON fragment would break the target schema; observed behavior: with mode=warn we emit a warning event in the stream and continue; with mode=enforce the stream terminates with a structured error and a resume token for clients that want to retry with permissive mode.
- Function call fence tests simulate malformed function args; the call is blocked and an action-level diagnostic is returned.
- We ran the change against the main CI matrix; two unrelated flaky e2e tests were retriggered and both passed on rerun.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default remains permissive to avoid breaking existing customers.
- Feature-flag rollout across dedicated clusters for 48h, followed by gradual rollout to hosted API.
- SDKs will add helpers to surface new error_type codes; PRs for python/ts sdks will follow in a separate change (linked in linear).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide whether buffer-and-repair should be multi-pass for certain schemas (performance trade-off).
- Consider exposing structured 'stream events' for warnings to the Console/Observability so customers can alert on schema warnings.

Related: ENG-1429 (streaming schema deliverable), SUP-4052 (customer reported misrouted function call in streaming), ENG-1581 (openai compat error taxonomy).

discussion: Eve Nakamura: Nice separation of concerns. Two questions: 1) what's the expected CPU impact for high qps streaming endpoints? 2) do we need an opt-in header for Dedicated customers?

Aisha Patel: Answered: we measured ~2-3% additional CPU at 1k qps with sentence-boundary checkpoints; we will gate via runtime.output_policy.enabled and expose runtime flag for Dedicated clusters. Added perf measurements in a follow-up benchmark PR.

Diego Morales: Can we avoid duplicating validators? The change looks like it references the same compiled validator but make that explicit in the code comments. Also please add a test for large arrays where checkpoint heuristics might split mid-structure.
Aisha Patel: Added code comment and unit test for large-array checkpointing (tests/unit/test_checkpoint_large_array.rs).
